title: Apple's LG Smart-Home Gear Gets Exclusive iPhone Proximity Feature
excerpt: Code found in iOS 27 shows iPhones will detect Apple's co-developed LG accessories on tap, popping a Dynamic Island hint for instant controls — as Apple stages a "Welcome home" event on October 13.
body:
• Apple is adding an iPhone-only trick to its upcoming LG-built smart-home gear: code in iOS 27 reveals "Proximity Control" — tap an iPhone near an accessory and the Dynamic Island pops up a hint with an "Open Controls" button, or a camera viewer for doorbells and cameras.
  • The hardware deal is "second-party": Bloomberg reports Apple spent months co-developing the accessories with LG Electronics, which will sell them under LG's name and handle manufacturing and support, while Apple owns design and software.
  • Don't expect to buy any of it on October 13: development has reportedly slipped, so the video doorbell, smart deadbolt, round Nest-like thermostat, sensors, and cameras may not reach buyers until early 2027.
  • What this means for you: Apple's "Welcome home" event this Tuesday will likely frame the whole HomeKit reboot, but the LG accessories are months out — and the tap-to-control perks are gated to iPhone and HomeKit, not standard Matter, so cross-platform smart-home owners will get the same hardware with a thinner experience.

Apple's smart-home comeback keeps gaining detail. Days before the company's "Welcome home" event on Tuesday, October 13, code researcher @itspdfu has found a new iPhone-exclusive feature buried in iOS 27 code and the accessories' device firmware: "Proximity Control," which lets iPhone users tap or bring their phone near one of Apple's upcoming LG-built accessories and get an instant control hint out of the Dynamic Island.

According to the findings, reported by 9to5Mac, MacRumors, and AppleInsider, thermostats and similar devices will trigger a Dynamic Island hint with an "Open Controls" button, while cameras and the video doorbell will surface a live camera viewer. During first-time setup, tapping an accessory pops the Dynamic Island into pairing feedback, mirroring the tap-to-pair behavior Apple built for the HomePod. iPhones without a Dynamic Island and iPads get a 30-second notification instead, and the whole feature can be disabled in the Home app. The implementation is still being revised across betas and could change before shipping.

Context & Background

The feature matters because of what's behind the hardware. Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reported that Apple spent months co-developing connected-home accessories with LG Electronics — but the products will carry LG's name, not Apple's. LG handles manufacturing and customer support; Apple's role is design and software. Bloomberg describes the arrangement as "second-party." LG has already started the regulatory approval process — FCC filings exist — and Apple's involvement appears nowhere in them.

"Bloomberg describes the arrangement as "second-party." LG has already started the regulatory approval process — FCC filings exist — and Apple's involvement appears nowhere in them."

https://youtube.com/watch?v=9uZUGudjsDg

The reported range covers the categories that actually sell: a video doorbell, a smart deadbolt lock, a round, Nest-like smart thermostat (Matter/Thread/Wi-Fi/BLE), temperature/humidity sensors, an indoor camera, an outdoor camera, and a floodlight camera. That's the context for this whole push: HomeKit launched in 2014, and Apple let it drift while Amazon's Ring and Google's Nest took the doorbell, lock, thermostat, and camera categories. Gurman frames the LG deal as a formal HomeKit reboot — and the iOS 27 code suggests the reboot ships with iPhone-exclusive perks baked in.

Impact & Analysis

The technical mechanism is the interesting part for the industry. The accessory writes an "apple-deviceid" into the Matter payload on its NFC tag and broadcasts a Bluetooth Low Energy advertisement for Apple Proximity Control. LG's firmware — for the lock and thermostat, which identify an NXP SE051H Secure Element — replaces NXP's standard Matter NFC applet with a HomeKit applet. Translation: NFC tap-to-setup is HomeKit-exclusive, even though iOS 27 also supports standard Matter NFC. Conventional Matter pairing remains available once the device is powered on: tap the iPhone, pair over HomeKit NFC, store credentials in the NFC secure element, power on, join Wi-Fi or Thread, and let the home hub finish Matter setup.

https://x.com/itspdfu/status/2108555274357199138

The exclusivity is a familiar Apple move — hardware partnerships that keep the best bits inside the ecosystem — but the code table in iOS 27 suggests the program is bigger than LG. The "second-party" table covers ten products so far: LG's smart thermostat, a GEMS smart thermostat, a smart deadbolt, a GEMS smart door lock, and temperature/humidity sensors in standard and GEMS versions. It also lists Schneider Electric devices — two thermostat variants, a temperature/humidity sensor, and a possible fourth sensor variant — suggesting the program extends beyond LG, as AppleInsider's Wesley Hilliard reported. GEMS branding points at LG's German-market hardware division, hinting the lineup is being built for international distribution from day one.

Diaspora Angle

For Apple-ecosystem users in India and among NRIs, the interesting wrinkle is the name on the box: LG is one of the strongest household brands in India, so an LG-branded thermostat or doorbell walks into Indian homes far more naturally than an Apple one would — even as the iPhone-exclusive perks keep the lineup an Apple-first buy.

What's Next

The timeline is now the open question. Apple announced the October 13 "Welcome home" event, where it is expected to show a smart-home hub (reportedly with a roughly six-inch square display, in tabletop and wall-mounted versions, handling lights, locks, video calls, music, and photos), an updated Apple TV 4K, and a refreshed HomePod mini — the HomePod mini 2 reportedly gets a faster chip for Siri AI (the current model runs on the S5 chip from the Apple Watch Series 5) and new colors: pink, white, green, blue, and black.

But the LG accessories are a different story. Development has reportedly slipped, and they may not reach buyers until early 2027 — at least a few months out. Expect October 13 to frame the strategy and the iPhone integration; expect the hardware itself to follow well after the holidays.
